body:
A `FieldTimeSeries` can be the condition of a boundary condition on the ice velocities, thickness or concentration, for example to prescribe the ice at an open boundary from a dataset. Two things keep it from working with a partly resident series (`InMemory(N)`):

- `update_model_field_time_series!` collects series from `model.tracers`, `model.external_heat_fluxes`, `model.snowfall` and `model.dynamics`, but not from `model.velocities`, `model.ice_thickness` or `model.ice_concentration`. Their boundary series are never updated, so the window stays at the frames it was built with.
- `update_state!` updates the series after `fill_halo_regions!`, so the halos would be filled from the window of the previous time.

This PR adds the three prognostic fields to the search (Oceananigans already finds series held by a field's boundary conditions) and moves the update to the start of `update_state!`.

## Tests

A new test in the `timestepping` group drives the east boundary of `h` with a series read from disk with `InMemory(2)` and checks the halo after each of four steps. On `main` it errors at the second step with a `BoundsError`, reading frame 3 of the two-frame window; with this change it passes. The `timestepping`, `lateral_boundary_conditions`, `advection` and `checkpointing` groups pass on CPU.

title: Advance time series held by the prognostic fields' boundary conditions
